curation.notes: Magnetic tweezers assay measuring the mechanical stability and kinetics of human PARP1 and PARP2 bridging the two ends of a DNA double-strand break in a PEG-DNA construct tethered between a coverslip and an M-280 streptavidin Dynabead. Rotating magnet configuration allows supercoiling to test restoration of torsional continuity; different DSB overhang types compared. No AFM is used despite the auto-assigned secondary technique.

evidence.snippet: All experiments were conducted at room temperature (22 ± 1) °C.
The magnetic beads were tracked in real time at 20 frames per second using a previously described video image analysis algorithm (46) with custom C++ and LabVIEW (National Instruments) software.

bead_size.note: nominal diameter of the named M-280 bead product; not stated numerically in the text

evidence.snippet: Superparamagnetic beads (M-280 streptavidin Dynabeads, ThermoFisher) were incubated with gel-purified DNA constructs before introducing into the flow-cell.

handle_sequences.annotations: a 20 kDa bis-azide PEG was reacted overnight with a Dibenzocyclooctyne (DBCO) modified oligonucleotide before agarose gel purification

evidence.snippet: The full-length DNA construct was then generated in a golden-gate assembly reaction (44) with PCR amplicons before a final agarose gel purification.
Human PARP1 and PARP2 proteins were made using a baculovirus expression system and purified by Immobilized Metal Affinity Chromatography (IMAC) affinity and size-exclusion chromatography
We find that PARP2 forms a remarkably stable mechanical link (rupture force ~85 pN) across blunt-end 5'-phosphorylated DSBs and restores torsional continuity allowing DNA supercoiling.
Tests of T4 DNA ligase (Fig. 3) were performed in 1× NEB CutSmart (−ATP buffer) or 1× NEB T4 ligase buffer (+ATP buffer) with a concentration of 10 U/μL.
